executive_summary.description: Phase C20 successfully executed the authorized Tier-1 zero-compute cross-domain evaluation with zero training, zero Kaggle execution, and zero HOLDOUT access. However, forensic post-audit reveals three epistemic overclaims in the narrative report: (1) an overgeneralized input normalization superiority claim refuted by EVAL-A machine data; (2) an unsupported causal claim attributing OPS-02 performance bounds to domain properties rather than optimization; and (3) an overextended '100% bug-free' claim. All three claims are formally rectified herein against Level 5 machine truth.

forensic_corrections.target_claim: Model-declared normalization yielded consistently superior transfer fidelity across all evaluated models.
forensic_corrections.corrected_epistemic_position: Input normalization transfer sensitivity is EVALUATION-DEPENDENT. In EVAL-A, target-native normalization outperformed model-declared normalization (0.028818 vs 0.027285). In EVAL-B and EVAL-C, model-declared normalization outperformed target-native normalization. Normalization cannot be claimed to be universally superior across domain transfers.

forensic_corrections.target_claim: OPS-02 performance is fundamentally bounded by dataset domain properties rather than an optimization failure.
forensic_corrections.level_5_machine_truth: Cross-domain evaluation provides observational transfer degradation data only. It does not manipulate or isolate optimization mechanisms (such as class-loss weighting, gradient competition, or capacity).
forensic_corrections.corrected_epistemic_position: Tier-1 cross-domain evaluation demonstrates substantial transfer degradation and heterogeneous class-level behavior across domains. It provides descriptive evidence regarding cross-domain generalization, but does NOT identify the causal source of the OPS-02 development performance limitation.

forensic_corrections.target_claim: The OPS-02 inference and evaluation pipeline is 100% bug-free and robust.
forensic_corrections.level_5_machine_truth: Phase C20 passed 72 automated guardrails testing specific audited invariants and protocol checks.
forensic_corrections.corrected_epistemic_position: The evaluation pipeline is 'verified against the implemented C20 guardrail suite and audited invariants.' Automated tests verify that checked properties hold; they do not establish universal absence of defects or universal robustness across untested scenarios.

forensic_corrections.target_claim: Ambiguity regarding whether historical C16 ran on an obsolete or unpatched dataset compared to canonical v1.0.1.

level_5_machine_truth.split_allocations: 132 TRAIN / 40 DEV / 40 HOLDOUT identical across both
level_5_machine_truth.documentation_patch: v1.0.1 corrected a textual transcription typo (from 41/39 to 40/40 DEV/HOLDOUT) without altering a single byte of dataset files.

forensic_corrections.corrected_epistemic_position: Historical C16 data identity was OPS02_v1.0.0_FROZEN, and its physical raster and mask contents are bitwise identical to OPS02_v1.0.1_FROZEN. We preserve C16's historical provenance while establishing v1.0.1 as the canonical specification identity. Do not retroactively rewrite historical execution records.

forensic_corrections.target_claim: C8 and C10 historical runs provide an isolated measurement of random seed variance on OPS-01.
forensic_corrections.level_5_machine_truth: While C8 used seed 42 and C10 used seed 101, historical run logs indicate that C8 and C10 executions may contain additional environmental and execution differences.
forensic_corrections.corrected_epistemic_position: Existing C8/C10 historical runs do not provide a clean isolated estimate of seed variance unless machine evidence proves that all other execution and environmental conditions were strictly identical. Seed variance on OPS-01 remains an unisolated observation.
